questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.9 Gemini Cost & Capacity | Trigger #22 | M3L5 Slide 16
questions.q: How are tokens used to CREATE a context cache billed in Gemini for implicit versus explicit caching?
options: Billed at the standard input token price for BOTH implicit and explicit caching (neither free nor double price)
Cache creation is completely free for both implicit and explicit caching
Cache creation is billed at 2x the standard input price for explicit caching only
Cache creation is billed at the output token price
questions.why: Per §1.9 & Trigger #22: Tokens used to create a cache are billed at the standard input price for BOTH implicit and explicit caching. Watch out for traps saying 'Cache creation is free' or 'double price.'

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.9 Gemini Cost & Capacity | Self-Test #7 & Trigger #22 | M3L5 Slides 16–17
questions.q: What is the billing difference between Explicit Caching and Implicit Caching for cache STORAGE, and what discount do cached reads receive on Gemini 2.5+ models?
options: Explicit caching charges storage based on TTL; implicit caching has NO storage cost; cached reads receive ~90% discount on Gemini 2.5+ models
Implicit caching charges TTL storage; explicit caching has no storage cost; cached reads receive a 10% discount
Both explicit and implicit caching charge hourly TTL storage fees
Neither explicit nor implicit caching offers a discount on cached read tokens
questions.why: Per §1.9 & Self-Test #7: Explicit caching charges storage based on TTL (how long the cache is kept), whereas implicit caching has NO storage cost. Cached reads get ~90% discount on Gemini 2.5+ models.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.9 & §6.2 | Trigger #22 | M3L5 Slide 17
questions.q: What are the minimum token thresholds for context caching on Gemini 2.5 Flash versus Gemini 3.x Flash?
options: Gemini 2.5 Flash = 2,048 tokens; Gemini 3.x Flash = 4,096 tokens
Both models require a minimum of 100,000 tokens
Gemini 2.5 Flash = 32,768 tokens; Gemini 3.x Flash = 128 tokens
There is no minimum token threshold for any Gemini model
questions.why: Per §1.9 & §6.2 (Trigger #22): Minimum tokens for caching vary by model—Gemini 2.5 Flash is 2,048 tokens, and Gemini 3.x Flash is 4,096 tokens.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.9 Gemini Cost & Capacity | Trigger #22 | M3L5 Slides 15, 18
questions.q: Which statement accurately describes what Vertex AI Provisioned Throughput (PT) supports and does NOT support?
options: PT supports fine-tuned models, but does NOT support batch prediction and does NOT cover calls made by other Agent Platform products (e.g., Agent Search) even when using the same model
PT covers batch prediction jobs and all Agent Search queries automatically, but does not support fine-tuned models
PT only works for batch prediction and cannot be used for real-time online traffic
PT is only available for third-party open-source models on GKE
questions.why: Per §1.9 & Trigger #22: Provisioned Throughput supports fine-tuned models, but does NOT support batch prediction and does NOT cover calls made by other Agent Platform products (such as Agent Search) even with the same model.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.9 & §6.2 Semantic Routing | M3L5 Slide 19
questions.q: How does Semantic Routing reduce total Gemini inference spend without sacrificing quality on hard tasks, and what are the 5 Gemini Consumption Tiers?
options: Routes simple queries to Flash-Lite and complex queries to Pro (~3x cost gap); the 5 tiers are Provisioned Throughput, Standard PayGo, Priority PayGo, Flex PayGo, and Batch Inference (50% discount)
Routes all queries to Gemini Ultra; the 5 tiers are Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, and Diamond
Truncates every user prompt to 10 tokens; the 5 tiers are Dev, Test, Stage, Prod, and Archive
Disables system prompts on weekends
questions.why: Per §1.9 & §6.2 (M3L5 Slides 15, 19): Semantic routing sends simple queries to Flash-Lite and complex ones to Pro. The 5 consumption tiers are: 1. Provisioned Throughput, 2. Standard PayGo, 3. Priority PayGo, 4. Flex PayGo, and 5. Batch Inference (50% discount).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.10 GE Connectors | Trigger #10 | M1L6 Slides 6, 10, 16
questions.q: Users complain that when they query Microsoft SharePoint through a Gemini Enterprise Federated Connector, they are prompted for a second Microsoft sign-in. Why does this happen?
options: It is expected behavior (not a misconfiguration): Federated connectors query Microsoft live with the user's delegated permissions so SharePoint enforces that user's current ACLs; Workforce Identity Federation does NOT remove it
Workforce Identity Federation (WIF) is misconfigured; enabling WIF eliminates the second sign-in prompt
The SharePoint data store is corrupted and needs to be re-indexed into BigQuery
Model Armor is blocking the OAuth redirect URL
questions.why: Per §1.10 & Trigger #10: The second sign-in is NOT a misconfiguration. Federated connectors query Microsoft live using the user's delegated OAuth token so SharePoint enforces real-time ACLs (no stale index). Deploying WIF does NOT remove the second sign-in.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.10 BigQuery ObjectRef | Trigger #20 | M3L4 Slide 14
questions.q: What is a BigQuery 'ObjectRef' column used for in multimodal agent architectures, and what are its four STRUCT fields?
options: A STRUCT of 'uri', 'version', 'authorizer' (Cloud resource connection), and 'details' (managed metadata: content type, size, hash, updated)—it does NOT cache object bytes and is NOT a signed URL
A BLOB column that caches the raw MP4/PDF file bytes directly inside BigQuery storage
A temporary pre-signed HTTP URL that expires after 15 minutes
A foreign key that points only to Cloud Spanner tables
questions.why: Per §1.10 & Trigger #20 (M3L4 Slide 14): ObjectRef is a STRUCT of 'uri', 'version', 'authorizer' (the Cloud resource connection BigQuery uses to reach the object), and 'details' (content type, size, hash, updated). Watch out for traps saying it caches bytes or is a signed URL.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §6.6 & §5 Trigger #9 | M1L5 Slides 3, 17–18, 22
questions.q: What are the 4 phases of the Google Cloud Migration Framework (in exact order), and what advantages does Cloud Run offer when migrating from AWS Lambda?
options: 1. Assess → 2. Plan & Build → 3. Migrate → 4. Optimize; Cloud Run is container-based (any language), supports up to 60-min timeout (vs Lambda's 15-min limit), and handles concurrent requests per instance
1. Estimate → 2. Discover → 3. Assess → 4. Plan → 5. Migrate; Cloud Run has a 5-min timeout limit
1. Prepare → 2. Scan → 3. Remediate → 4. Monitor; Cloud Run requires rewriting all code in Go
1. Spec → 2. Scaffold → 3. Build → 4. Deploy; Cloud Run charges 24/7 even when idle
questions.why: Per Trigger #9 & §6.6 (M1L5 Slides 3, 17–18): The 4-Phase Migration Framework is 1. Assess → 2. Plan & Build → 3. Migrate → 4. Optimize (don't confuse with the 5-step Migration Center journey). Cloud Run beats Lambda with container portability, up to 60-min timeout vs 15-min, and multi-request concurrency.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §6.6 google-agents-cli | M0L3 Slide 63
questions.q: What is the correct 8-stage agent development lifecycle supported by 'google-agents-cli' (M0L3 Slide 63)?
options: Spec → Scaffold → Build → Orchestrate → Evaluate → Deploy → Publish → Observe
Plan → Code → Zip → Upload → Bill → Delete → Archive → Repeat
Register → Discover → Govern → Orchestrate → Prepare → Scan → Remediate → Monitor
Assess → Plan & Build → Migrate → Optimize → Span → Trace → Session → Task
questions.why: Per §6.6 (M0L3 Slide 63): The 8 stages of google-agents-cli are Spec → Scaffold → Build → Orchestrate → Evaluate → Deploy → Publish → Observe.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — Tab 3 M0L2 Slide 8
questions.q: When scoping an enterprise agentic AI business case with a customer (Module 0), what is the recommended 4-step value-framing sequence?
options: 1. Define Business KPI → 2. Define Cost Per Task (not cost per token) → 3. Calculate Expected Savings → 4. Frame Value vs. Spend
1. Quote cost per 1M tokens → 2. Pick the largest model → 3. Buy GPUs → 4. Define KPIs next year
1. Deploy to GKE → 2. Enable Basic SDP → 3. Run CodeMender → 4. Measure token count
1. Migrate from AWS → 2. Enable SharePoint connector → 3. Create ObjectRef → 4. Close deal
questions.why: Per Tab 3 (Module 0 Scoping): Frame business value around Cost Per Task (not raw cost per token): 1. Define Business KPI → 2. Define Cost Per Task → 3. Calculate Expected Savings → 4. Frame Value vs. Spend.
